reference.title: Band Reverse Spider Curl
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (the proxy refused gymvisual.com), so the movement follows the name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, 0.3 s squeeze, about 2.3 s down

prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen; start light, the overhand grip is weaker than the palm-up grip
prescription.progression: Band tension is user-chosen: pick a band you can curl for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion); add reps, then a stronger band or a shorter grip on the band.

cues.text: Loop the band low round a rack upright in front of the bench. Set the back pad low, about 30 degrees; lie chest-down with the shoulders over the top edge, feet planted behind, arms hanging straight down, holding the band with palms facing back.
Breathe out and curl up, knuckles leading; the upper arms stay perpendicular to the floor.
Squeeze at the top for a moment; wrists straight, knuckles up.
Breathe in and lower slowly against the band to straight arms.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows drifting forward toward the head
mistakes.fix: Keep the upper arms pointing straight at the floor.

mistakes.mistake: Wrists bending down (knuckles dropping) as the hands rise
mistakes.fix: Keep the wrists straight, in line with the forearms; use a lighter band.

mistakes.mistake: Partial reps near the top only
mistakes.fix: Straighten the arms fully each rep.

mistakes.mistake: Lifting the chest off the pad
mistakes.fix: Keep the chest on the pad throughout.

kinematics.norm: Full range: mean elbow range was about 117-123 degrees across barbell, EZ-bar and alternating dumbbell curls (Marcolin 2018)

kinematics.measure: Forearm rotation (wrist pron channel, 0 = palm up/forward, 90 = thumb up)
kinematics.norm: Pronated grip: biceps activity in the lifting phase was about 19% lower than with the supinated grip, so the brachioradialis and brachialis share more of the work (Coratella 2023)

kinematics.measure: Upper arm from the trunk line (sagittal)
kinematics.norm: Upper arms vertical, so the shoulder is flexed about 60 degrees from the trunk on a 30-degree pad (Moon 2013 found biceps activity highest near 75 degrees of shoulder flexion)
Controlled, about 1 s up and 2-3 s down (clinical opinion); biceps activity was lower while lowering than lifting at the same load (Oliveira 2009)

Elastic tension rises as the band stretches, so the load is highest where the band is longest; at matched effort, elastic tubing and dumbbells gave similar muscle activity in upper-body exercises (Andersen 2010); anchored low in front, the band pulls down and forward on the hands, so it resists the whole arc of the curl
Low incline, about 30-45 degrees, chest at the top edge (common practice, clinical opinion)

kinematics.measure: Chest on the pad (skinned mesh gap)
kinematics.norm: Chest on the pad, shoulders at the top edge, feet planted (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #16971, Band Reverse Spider Curl, video (movement reference)

cautions: Elbow or wrist pain: use a lighter band and shorten the range; stop if pain is sharp (clinical opinion).
Keep the wrists straight (in line with the forearm) (clinical opinion).
Check the band for nicks or tears before each set and make sure it cannot slip off its anchor (under the feet, round the upright).
Neck strain: keep the head in line with the trunk rather than looking up (clinical opinion).
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Chest pressure: raise the pad to 45 degrees.
Wrist discomfort with the palms down: neutral (hammer) grip.
progressions: Stronger band, or anchor further from the bench.

muscleNotes.biceps_r: Still flexes the elbow, though less than with the palms up (Coratella 2023); the brachialis (not a separate id on this rig) works hard whatever the grip. With the upper arms hanging in front of the head line the biceps works with the shoulder flexed (Moon 2013).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Still flexes the elbow, though less than with the palms up (Coratella 2023); the brachialis (not a separate id on this rig) works hard whatever the grip. With the upper arms hanging in front of the head line the biceps works with the shoulder flexed (Moon 2013).
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_r: Brachioradialis and the wrist extensors (mapped to the forearm extensor region): with the palms down the brachioradialis takes a larger share of the elbow flexion and the wrist extensors hold the wrist straight; biceps activity was about 19% lower than with a supinated grip (Coratella 2023).
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_l: Brachioradialis and the wrist extensors (mapped to the forearm extensor region): with the palms down the brachioradialis takes a larger share of the elbow flexion and the wrist extensors hold the wrist straight; biceps activity was about 19% lower than with a supinated grip (Coratella 2023).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Holds the upper arms vertical; the elbows must not drift forward.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Holds the upper arms vertical; the elbows must not drift forward.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk still on the pad.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Keep the shoulder blades set so the shoulders do not sag toward the floor.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Keep the shoulder blades set so the shoulders do not sag toward the floor.
